subject: Spike in 429s & latency — Novus Health production
messages:
From: Kevin O'Neal <kevin.oneal@novus-health.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: Sara Kim <sara.kim@novus-health.com>, sre@novus-health.com
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 12:15:00 -0400
Subject: Production spike: 429s and 600ms+ p95s (urgent)

Hi Naomi,

We're seeing a sudden surge in 429s and elevated p95 latency across our production requests to your API starting around 07:45 PDT. Error rate climbed from ~0.5% to 6% and user-impacted traffic rolled back two scheduled jobs. Attached is a filtered traffic dump (novus-traffic-log-20260803.csv) showing request timestamps, model, route, and the 429/500 responses.

Can you confirm whether any rate limit or burst policy changes occurred on your side in the last 24 hours? Our team had no config changes. This is causing degraded UX for our telehealth flows — we need an ETA on mitigation and whether you'll take any rollbacks.

Kevin
SRE Lead, Novus Health
kevin.oneal@novus-health.com
+1 415-555-0192

[Attachment: novus-traffic-log-20260803.csv]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin O'Neal <kevin.oneal@novus-health.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 12:34:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: 429s and 600ms+ p95s (urgent)

Hi Kevin — thanks for the signal and the logs.

Short answer: we saw a configuration push to burst/quota rules targeting the "production" tenant group at ~07:30 PDT this morning. I'm pulling the change diff and asking infra to evaluate rollback now. I'll confirm whether the push included an unintended per-tenant cap.

Next steps I'm initiating:
- Marcus is triaging kernel/queue saturation and policy diffs (cc'd).
- I'll propose an immediate rollback of the burst policy if infra confirms it's the cause.
- Can we get a short call at 13:00 PDT to align on impact window and any required credits?

Apologies for the disruption — we'll treat this as P1 and follow up with a timeline.

Naomi
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0133

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: 429s and 600ms+ p95s (urgent)

Naomi / Marissa — quick technical note from infra: we pushed an aggressive burst suppression tweak to reduce noisy-tenant spikes last night at 23:10 PDT. The new config lowers max_burst_tokens and changes the token refill window from 1s -> 5s for the "production" route. That could explain elevated 429s when sustained fanout occurs.

I've attached the policy diff (redwood-policy-diff.patch). For immediate mitigation I recommend:
1) revert the max_burst_tokens to previous value (rollback id: roll-20260803-01) — low risk and should restore behavior.
2) enable temporary per-tenant quota leniency for Novus (30m window) while we monitor.

I'll coordinate rollback with deployments and confirm when done.

Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime Operations
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood-policy-diff.patch]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin O'Neal <kevin.oneal@novus-health.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 13:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: 429s and 600ms+ p95s (urgent)

Hi Kevin — we pushed the rollback at 13:15 PDT and enabled a temporary per-tenant leniency window for Novus for 30 minutes. Early telemetry shows error rate dropping back to baseline and p95 latency returning to expected ranges.

What we observed:
- A burst policy change extended the refill window (1s -> 5s), which caused sustained multi-worker bursts to consume tokens more slowly and trigger 429s under sustained fanout.
- The rollback reverted max_burst_tokens and restored original refill timing.

Request from our side: can you confirm whether consumer job retries are still spiking? If you can share a short sample of the retry pattern (timestamps + route) we'll correlate.

Also, Marissa and I will set up an exec-facing RCA and a short mutual action plan:
- 48h monitoring watch with logs shared
- Policy change gating for high-impact routes
- Retro and compensation review (we can discuss credits)

Proposed call: 14:00 PDT today — will send calendar invite if that works.

Naomi

Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production spike: 429s and 600ms+ p95s (post-incident summary & next steps)

Kevin / Sara — thanks again for the patience. Quick summary and next steps: 

Incident summary (short):
- Impact window: 07:30 PDT — 13:15 PDT on 2026-08-03.
- Root cause: mis-specified burst/refill policy pushed to production for "production" tenant group (regression from a safety tweak). The 5s refill window + lowered max_burst_tokens led to token exhaustion under sustained multi-worker fanout and generated elevated 429s.
- Mitigation: rollback (roll-20260803-01) at 13:15 PDT and temporary per-tenant leniency. Error rate normalized within ~10 minutes of rollback.

Action items (agreed):
- Redwood: final RCA and postmortem by EOD Friday (we attached a draft postmortem — postmortem-draft.docx).
- Redwood: implement a policy-change gating workflow (policy-change playbook + automated preflight that simulates worst-case fanout) by 2026-08-20.
- Novus: provide retry pattern sample for 07:30-09:30 PDT to ensure there are no client-side hotspots.
- Commercial: we'll apply a one-time credit for the impacted usage while we finalize the RCA (Marissa will coordinate).

Please find attached the logs we used to verify rollback. If you want, Marissa and I can present the technical RCA to your SRE/engineering leadership next week.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0133
